Marissa — draft below (will attach a longer doc before kickoff):

Options for backfill (pros/cons & cost):

1) Bulk re-encode + full rebuild (recommended for initial migration)
   - Pros: simplest, single consistent index, easier validation.
   - Cons: peak GPU and I/O load during the window; requires downtime or parallel index approach.
   - Estimate: ~1.2M docs x median 150 tokens => ~180M tokens. With a quantized 7B model and a batch encoder we estimate 30–40 GPU hours on A10p-class nodes (with our batching).

2) Streaming (incremental) re-encode using nightly workers
   - Pros: spreads cost, minimal peak load.
   - Cons: longer time to parity; complexity in ensuring identical embeddings if encoding parameters change.

3) Hybrid: seed core index (100k high-quality docs) then streaming for the rest — good middle ground.

Vector DB considerations:
- Pinecone: great managed ops, consistent latency, but cost grows with replicas.
- Redis Vector (managed): super-fast for low-latency queries; need careful sharding for scale.
- Milvus (self-hosted): cheapest at scale but requires infra ops and attention to compaction.

Rerank eval plan (short):
- Create 1k query set: 800/100/100 split for train/val/test.
- Metrics: Precision@5, MRR@10, NDCG@10, and a side-by-side human judgment set (200 queries) for quality regressions.
- Baseline: existing prototype + new index + reranker thresholds.

I will attach an initial cost estimate and a script to profile backfill throughput by EOD Friday.

—Rishi
